Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Krishna answers that both He and Arjuna have passed through countless births, but while Krishna retains full, flawless memory of all of them, Arjuna cannot remember.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Distinguishing the unlimited, omniscient nature of the Divine from the conditioned, forgetful nature of the soul.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna clarifies: 'bahuni me vyatitani janmani tava carjuna, tany aham veda sarvani na tvam vettha parantapa' (Many births both you and I have passed; I know all of them, but you do not).
Outcome/Resolution: Reveals the soul's conditioned limits while establishing Krishna's supreme omniscience and eternal memory.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Memory and Consciousness Limits: Recognizing the natural constraints of human cognitive recall
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Finite vs. Infinite Identity: Distinguishing between temporary roles and continuous awareness
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Accepting Human Limitations: Embracing human boundaries without losing sight of divine connection

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Bahuni me vyatitani janmani (Many births have passed for both of us)
Tany aham veda sarvani na tvam vettha (I remember all of them, but you do not)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna explains that both the Divine and the living entity are eternal, but while conditioned souls forget past lives due to body changes, the Lord retains complete, uninterrupted memory.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Human perception and memory are selective and bounded by physical constraints; recognizing our limited perspective helps cultivate intellectual humility and reliance on higher guidance.
